image.subject: A dusty wooden board sidewalk in a small Missouri river town in summer, heat shimmering over the street, a whitewashed picket fence running beside it.

storyboard.claim: The story opens in a hot, sleepy river town in St. Petersburg.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Empty board sidewalk and whitewashed fence in blazing summer heat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opening.
storyboard.addedInformation: Setting: 1840s Missouri river town.

image.subject: A sun-bleached street of a Missouri town at high noon, the air thick with heat, a dog sprawled in the shade of a wooden porch.

storyboard.claim: The heat is heavy and oppressive, the kind that makes labour feel worse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Glaring noon sun, shade-seeking dog, still air.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the setting of the hot street.
storyboard.addedInformation: Mood: oppressive midwestern summer heat.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, a grin that is half mischief, a tin bucket or whitewash brush in hand, staring up at a long broadboard fence nine feet high.

storyboard.claim: Tom faces a fence that looks endless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom, small against a tall broad-board fence, staring up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the boy and the fence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fence height of nine feet.

storyboard.claim: The chore is enormous: thirty yards of fence, nine feet high, one bucket of whitewash.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three short text lines, no image, the scale stated plainly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the numbers behind the boy's dread.
storyboard.addedInformation: Scale of the punishment.

image.subject: A stout, grey-haired woman of about sixty in a dark calico dress with a white collar and apron, spectacles on a cord, a wooden spoon or a switch in her hand, standing on a porch in the afternoon sun.

storyboard.claim: The fence is a penalty from Aunt Polly for skipping school and fighting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly with a switch, stern, on a porch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boy's dread is now tied to a person.
storyboard.addedInformation: Cause: skipped school and a fistfight that ruined his clothes.

image.subject: Four neighbourhood boys in patched shirts and bare feet line up along a whitewashed fence on a dusty street, one holding out a crisp apple, all waiting their turn with eager faces.

storyboard.claim: Hours later the chore has become a prize boys line up to win.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A queue of eager boys along a fence, one offering an apple.
storyboard.onScreenText: A TURN IS WORTH A FORTUNE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the reversal the narration promised.
storyboard.addedInformation: Boys pay for the chance to paint.

storyboard.claim: Neighbourhood kids beg and pay for a turn at the same fence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hosts trading banter, no picture needed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Banter reaction to the queue.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the line of boys.

left.label: THE PENALTY
left.subject: A miserable boy in patched trousers drags a whitewash brush along a fence at grim midday, the paint sagging in streaks.

right.label: THE PRIVILEGE
right.subject: Tom Sawyer in a faded blue shirt grins and steps back from a glossy fence as boys hold out coins and apples.

storyboard.claim: The same labour becomes a privilege once framed differently.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Split image: grim labour on the left, eager trade on the right.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the alchemy in the previous line.
storyboard.addedInformation: The same task, two framings.

image.subject: A quiet middle-aged man with a dark moustache in a dark suit and waistcoat, leaning on a writing desk with an open book, a half-smile.

storyboard.claim: The host welcomes viewers into a close reading of the book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator figure at a desk, half-smiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Host intro after the alchemy line.
storyboard.addedInformation: The narrator is introduced as the guide.

storyboard.claim: The book is Mark Twain's The Adventures of Tom Sawyer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A title document card with the book's name and author.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the book.
storyboard.addedInformation: Author and publication year.

image.subject: A middle-aged man in a dark suit reads a worn hardbound book at a library desk, a lamp throwing light across the open pages.

storyboard.claim: The analysis uses the text itself and a scholarly introduction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader at a lamp-lit library desk over an old book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Method of the analysis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sources: the text and a scholarly introduction.

left.label: THE POPULAR VIEW
left.subject: A bright, carefree riverbank with a barefoot boy and a fishing pole, sunlit willows and a lazy summer sky.

right.label: THE REAL BOOK
right.subject: The same riverbank under a heavy, watchful sky, with townspeople in a tight crowd staring at the water.

storyboard.claim: The popular picture of the book is almost entirely wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Split: a nostalgic riverbank versus a watchful, judging town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrast between popular memory and the text.

image.subject: A barefoot boy in patched trousers holds a cane fishing pole on a sunlit Mississippi riverbank, willows overhead, the water glinting.

storyboard.claim: Most people picture a harmless, nostalgic boy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A barefoot boy with a fishing pole by the river.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The popular image from the split.
storyboard.addedInformation: The nostalgic image of a fishing boy.

storyboard.claim: The argument is that the book is not about harmless fun.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bare question on screen, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: The thesis is stated as a question.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat with a neutral, thoughtful expression stands at the edge of a crowded board sidewalk, townspeople watching a boy pass.

storyboard.claim: The book studies how a whole society decides what matters.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An everyman at the edge of a watching crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: The town as a judging crowd.

storyboard.claim: The town decides what counts as work, play and a hero.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three words listed, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the three things the society defines.
storyboard.addedInformation: The three categories the book examines.

image.subject: An ordinary man in a plain grey coat holds a single gold coin on his open palm in a dusty town street, looking at it thoughtfully.

storyboard.claim: Value is not an inherent truth; it is something a community agrees to believe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man weighing one gold coin on his palm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the list into a principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gold coin as a symbol of agreed worth.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, sitting on a whitewashed fence with a grin, while boys hand him coins and apples.

storyboard.claim: Tom's real genius is persuading other boys to pay him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom on a fence, a line of boys handing over coins and apples.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names Tom's skill.
storyboard.addedInformation: Payment from the boys.

image.subject: A boy's hand takes a crisp apple from another boy, who grins while stepping away from a whitewashed fence on a sunny afternoon.

storyboard.claim: People pay him for the privilege of doing his own chores.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A snapshot-style photo of a trade of an apple for a turn at the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the persuasion with an example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Price paid: an apple, a coin.

storyboard.claim: The story unfolds in St. Petersburg, a sleepy Mississippi river town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A place caption card, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the setting as the arena.
storyboard.addedInformation: The town is the battlefield for social rules.

image.subject: A dusty street of a small river town where townspeople in Sunday clothes glance over whitewashed picket fences with stern, tight faces, heat rising off the road.

storyboard.claim: The town is a powder keg of social expectations.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stern townspeople watching over a fence on a hot street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the town's pressure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Social rules are watched by neighbours.

image.subject: A stout, grey-haired woman of about sixty in a dark calico dress with a white collar and apron, spectacles on a cord, a wooden spoon or a switch in her hand, standing firm in a doorway.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly embodies the strict Calvinist moral order.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly, firm, in a doorway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the moral order character.
storyboard.addedInformation: Calvinist moral authority.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly delivers grand monologues to force Tom into a compliant citizen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quoted line of moral instruction, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes how Polly pressures Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her method is lecturing.

image.subject: A slight, neat 9-year-old boy in a clean white shirt and pressed short trousers, hair combed flat, a prim and self-satisfied face, standing very straight.

storyboard.claim: Sid is the good child who does exactly as he is told.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sid, prim and neat, in a clean white shirt.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the good children.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sid as the model of obedience.

storyboard.claim: The good children have bought into the system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three checked text items, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists how Sid and Mary comply.
storyboard.addedInformation: The three marks of the compliant child.

image.subject: A thin, barefoot 13-year-old boy in ragged homespun clothes, a battered straw hat with a torn brim, standing beside an empty wooden hogshead barrel on a riverbank.

storyboard.claim: Huck sleeps in empty barrels and wears discarded men's clothes, an outcast on the fringe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Huck in ragged clothes beside an empty barrel.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts Huck with the good children.
storyboard.addedInformation: Huck's home is an empty barrel.

image.subject: A fair-haired 11-year-old girl in a pale blue dress with a white pinafore and a ribbon in her hair, shy eyes and a careful posture, standing in a timber doorway of a courthouse.

storyboard.claim: Becky sits at the centre of the social ladder as the judge's daughter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Becky, careful and shy, in a courthouse doorway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Places Becky at the top of the ladder.
storyboard.addedInformation: Her father is the judge.

left.label: SOCIETY'S PRICE
left.subject: Sunday school tickets stacked neatly on a wooden table beside an open Bible, arranged with great care.

right.label: TOM'S PRICE
right.subject: A boy's hand trades a crisp apple for a turn with a whitewash brush beside a half-painted fence.

storyboard.claim: Society sets the price, but the price is entirely made up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Split: ticket-and-Bible value versus an apple-for-a-turn trade.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the theme of agreed value.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two systems of worth side by side.

image.subject: A bright Saturday morning on a dusty town street, a whitewashed fence beside it, a group of free boys trotting past with fishing poles and swimming towels.

storyboard.claim: It is Saturday, and the free boys head off to play while Tom must work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boys with poles and towels pass the fence on a Saturday morning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the whitewashed fence scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Saturday is the day of play.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, sighing, dipping a whitewash brush into a bucket beside a fence.

storyboard.claim: Tom is miserable while the other boys play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sighing over the bucket, shoulders low.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's mood at the fence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's dejection.

image.subject: A round-faced 12-year-old boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, eating an apple, a cheerful and gullible grin, walking up the dusty street.

storyboard.claim: Ben Rogers arrives, eating an apple.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben with an apple, walking toward the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ben comes along the sidewalk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ben is eating a crisp apple.

image.subject: A round-faced boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, arms out, pretending to ring imaginary bells, apple in one hand, acting like a steamboat captain.

storyboard.claim: Ben imitates the steamboat Big Bizou, ringing imaginary bells.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben playing steamboat captain with arms out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ben's behaviour on the sidewalk.
storyboard.addedInformation: The steamboat Big Bizou.

image.subject: A steamboat on the broad brown Mississippi at dusk, its smoke drifting over the water toward the horizon.

storyboard.claim: The steamboat is the real model Ben is copying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A steamboat under smoke on the river.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the steamboat Ben imitates.
storyboard.addedInformation: The river steamboat as a symbol of play.

image.subject: A round-faced boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, laughing and pointing at a friend working at a fence, his apple still in hand.

storyboard.claim: Ben stops to mock Tom for having to work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben laughing and pointing at the working boy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ben turns his attention to Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mockery is the trigger for the trade.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, daintily sweeping a whitewash brush across a board, ignoring a boy at his side, a calm face.

storyboard.claim: Tom does not defend himself; he ignores Ben and paints daintily.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom painting calmly, not looking at Ben.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's reply to the mockery.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's psychology: no defence.

image.subject: A whitewash brush laid across a freshly painted board, the paint still wet and glistening in the afternoon sun, a neat stroke on the wood.

storyboard.claim: Tom treats the whitewashing like a literal masterpiece.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close view of a wet, carefully painted board.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the effect Tom is performing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The painting is staged as art.

storyboard.claim: Tom hesitates and plays hard to get when Ben asks to paint.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quoted line of refusal, no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: "NO, NO, I RECKON IT WOULDN'T HARDLY DO, BEN."
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ben asks to paint; Tom refuses.
storyboard.addedInformation: The quoted refusal is the hook.

image.subject: A stout, grey-haired woman in a dark calico dress with a white collar and apron, spectacles on a cord, inspecting a whitewashed picket fence with a critical eye, one hand on her hip.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly is particular about this fence, so only one boy in a thousand can do it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly critically inspecting the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Tom refuses.
storyboard.addedInformation: Polly's exacting standard is the pretext for scarcity.

storyboard.claim: Tom makes an abundant task look rare, creating artificial scarcity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stat card with the figures, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the scarcity mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Thirty yards of fence framed as a once-in-a-lifetime privilege.

storyboard.claim: Work is whatever you are obliged to do; play is whatever you are not obliged to do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A punchline card, no picture.
storyboard.onScreenText: WORK IS WHAT YOU MUST DO
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the scarcity idea into a rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chunk's core definition of work and play.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, stands unhurried beside a whitewashed picket fence with a brush in hand, glancing sideways at a boy who watches him, in the summer heat of a dusty St. Petersburg street.

storyboard.claim: Tom reframes the whitewashing as a rare privilege, flipping work into play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom painting slowly at the fence with a knowing sideways glance at an onlooker.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the fence scene: Tom has just decided the chore is a special honour.
storyboard.addedInformation: The attitude of the performance, not the labour itself, is what changes.

image.subject: Ben Rogers, a round-faced 12-year-old boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, hands his whole apple over to Tom Sawyer, a freckled boy in a faded blue shirt with bare feet, beside a whitewashed picket fence on a sunny street.

storyboard.claim: Ben is so captivated by the exclusivity that he gives away his apple for the chance to paint.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben handing an apple across the fence to Tom, a cheerful, gullible grin on Ben's face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom has framed the chore as a privilege; Ben now pays for it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ben's crisp apple is the price of a turn at the brush.

image.subject: A tired clerk in a dark coat sits at a timber writing desk in a plain office, a ledger open and untouched, while a colleague across the room leans back idly looking busy with a pen.

storyboard.claim: Workplaces often reward the look of hard work over actual results.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clerk who looks busy at a desk with nothing much done.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from Tom's fence to the listener's own working life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Appearance-over-results is applied to a modern-feeling office in period dress.

image.subject: A plain white linen shirt laid folded on a polished shop counter in a mid-1840s store, beside a small gilt-edged card reading a price far above its worth.

storyboard.claim: A plain shirt sold at a huge price purely because of its label and status.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A plain white shirt on a counter with an inflated price card beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The listener's example of the fence logic applied to a shop.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shirt is the same as any other; only the label makes it precious.

storyboard.claim: The same dynamic is at work in a specific logo on a plain item.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the sentence carries the idea alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Finishes the shop example in one line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the exact mechanism Twain is showing.

image.subject: A line of barefoot neighborhood boys waits along a whitewashed picket fence in the dusty sunlight, one of them holding a bright copper coin up toward the fence.

storyboard.claim: Value is driven entirely by perception and scarcity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A queue of boys eager for a turn at a fence, a coin held up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the earlier point with the scene of the fence line forming.
storyboard.addedInformation: The queue shows scarcity turning into demand.

image.subject: An early-morning dusty board sidewalk in St. Petersburg, Missouri, with a whitewashed picket fence beside it, a tin bucket set down on the boards and long shadows in the heat.

storyboard.claim: Tom tests the market theory earlier that same morning, before Ben arrives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty morning street with a bucket and fence, a place of earlier experiment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Steps back in time from the fence to the morning scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: The setting of the earlier economic experiment.

image.subject: A young barefoot boy in a ragged shirt and patched trousers carries a tin bucket along a dusty street toward the town pump, his shoulders bent under the bucket's weight.

storyboard.claim: Jim is fetching water from the town pump, a task Tom normally hates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A barefoot boy walking with a heavy tin bucket toward the pump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's earlier market test happens with this boy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The task is ordinary chore labour, carried by a child.

image.subject: A crowd of children gathered around an iron town pump on a dusty street in summer, some leaning on the post, some sitting on the edge of a trough, a few wrestling and laughing, buckets scattered.

storyboard.claim: The town pump is a busy social hub where children rest, trade and play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A crowd of children loitering at an iron pump, idle and lively.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pump is where the boy with the bucket is headed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows why the water run takes an hour.

image.subject: Children sit and stand in a loose circle on a dusty sidewalk by the pump, trading small playthings in their palms, bartering with raised hands, and a scuffle breaks out at the edge.

storyboard.claim: Getting one bucket of water takes an hour because of all the socializing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Children trading toys in a circle by the pump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the crowd at the pump into a trading scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: The delay is the social economy at work.

storyboard.claim: The water pump holds high social value, so Tom makes a trade there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a short confirmation line between the two speakers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A quick agreement that sets up Tom's offer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clarifies the pump's value in the story's own terms.

image.subject: A small white glass alley marble resting in a boy's open palm on a dusty sidewalk, a tin bucket beside it, bright summer light across the boards.

storyboard.claim: Tom offers his favourite possession, a white marble, for Jim's labour.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A white marble on an open palm, held out as a trade.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pump's social market now gets a direct material offer.
storyboard.addedInformation: The marble is Tom's most treasured item, which makes the offer large.

image.subject: A barefoot boy in a ragged shirt stands by a tin bucket and a whitewash brush, hesitating and eyeing a marble held out to him, his face torn between temptation and doubt.

storyboard.claim: Jim is tempted by the marble and the sore toe, and almost accepts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy hesitating over a held-out marble with a brush in his other hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The offer is on the table; the boy is wavering.
storyboard.addedInformation: The almost-deal is the hook before the interruption.

image.subject: A stout, grey-haired woman of about sixty in a dark calico dress with a white collar and apron, spectacles on a cord, sweeping a slipper through the air from a doorway, a shocked boy ducking at the edge of a whitewashed fence.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly steps in with a flying slipper and ends the transaction before it happens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly hurling a slipper from a doorway while the deal collapses.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The almost-deal is interrupted by the household authority.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that direct trade is shut down by the town's authorities.

image.subject: A sunlit backyard of a timber house behind a whitewashed picket fence, the kitchen door standing open, a single worn slipper lying in the dirt.

storyboard.claim: Authorities can crush a direct trade whenever they choose to intervene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty yard after the slipper has been thrown, the door still open.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The slipper has landed; the market is shut down.
storyboard.addedInformation: The aftermath, not the violence, is shown.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly regulated Tom's business out of existence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a rhetorical question carries the beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the crackdown with a wry summary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the outcome of the intervention.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer perched on the top rail of a whitewashed picket fence, chin in hand, a sly thoughtful look on his freckled face, the street quiet behind him.

storyboard.claim: After direct trade fails, Tom pivots to trading on psychology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sitting on a fence rail, thinking with a sly look.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The failed trade leads to a new plan.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's pivot is shown as a scheming pause.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer stands at a whitewashed picket fence in the afternoon sun, surrounded by a line of eager boys who hold out kites, marbles and bits of string as payment.

storyboard.claim: By the afternoon, Tom has turned the fence into a market and is rich.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at the fence while boys queue up with things to trade.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The psychological pivot has worked; the market is open.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom at the centre of an economy.

image.subject: A homemade paper kite with a long string flying high over a dusty small-town street in Missouri, a summer sky behind it.

storyboard.claim: One of Tom's payments is a kite, traded for turns at the fence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A kite in a bright sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first item in the list of payments.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kite is one of the goods Tom has collected.

image.subject: A dead grey rat hanging from a length of string tied to a picket fence rail, a broken piece of blue bottle glass lying on the dusty boards beside it.

storyboard.claim: Tom's collection includes a dead rat on a string and a blue bottle glass shard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A rat on a string and a blue glass shard on the boards.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list of treasures Tom has collected.
storyboard.addedInformation: The absurd value of the items is shown directly.

storyboard.claim: Tom's haul is an entire economy of odd treasures.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the list of items is the shape of the beat.
storyboard.onScreenText: KITE / DEAD RAT / 12 MARBLES / ONE-EYED KITTEN
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the list of payments from the afternoon market.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the full haul in one glance.

storyboard.claim: The objection: Tom is simply a lazy kid avoiding work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a real question is the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A speaker challenges the praise of Tom's economics.
storyboard.addedInformation: Raises the counter-argument that Tom is just lazy.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled boy in a faded blue shirt and bare feet, leans back lazily against a whitewashed picket fence with a brush dangling from one hand, a half-smile on his face.

storyboard.claim: On the surface Tom looks like a lazy boy dodging labour.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom lounging on the fence with a brush dangling loosely.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question with the surface picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the slacker reading of the scene.

storyboard.claim: Calling Tom an economic genius gives a middle-school con artist too much credit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a one-line punchline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection gets its sharpest form.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the critique as a joke.

image.subject: A close view of a freckled boy's hands gripping a whitewash brush, the brush loaded and moving across a picket board, the effort visible in his shoulders.

storyboard.claim: A closer look at Tom's actual effort shows he works hard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hands on a brush working a board.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the objection toward the real effort.
storyboard.addedInformation: Work is visible, not idle.

image.subject: Ben Rogers, a round-faced boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, paints a picket fence with a whitewash brush while Tom Sawyer, in a faded blue shirt and bare feet, stands nearby watching him work.

storyboard.claim: Tom does not walk away once Ben takes the brush.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben painting while Tom watches close by.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the effort point with a concrete scene of the handover.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom stays to supervise rather than leaving.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer sits on a wooden barrel in the shade of a tree beside a whitewashed fence, dangling his bare legs, munching an apple, his face relaxed and calculating.

storyboard.claim: Tom works twice as hard as manager of the operation than he would painting alone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom on a barrel in the shade with an apple.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The supervising Tom gets his own picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the management role and his apple.

image.subject: From behind, a freckled boy sits on a barrel in the shade, bare legs swinging, an apple in one hand, looking out over a row of other boys at a fence in the sun.

storyboard.claim: Tom sits in the shade actively planning more exploitation of innocence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy on a barrel looking over a line of boys at the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the barrel scene with the planning.
storyboard.addedInformation: The planning is seen in the watchful pose.

storyboard.claim: Tom must maintain the illusion of exclusivity for hours.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the sentence carries the idea alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the curation of the vibe.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the duration of the performance.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer leans against a picket fence with his arms folded and a feigned look of reluctance, while a new boy approaches holding out a kite and a dead rat on a string to bargain.

storyboard.claim: Each new boy triggers the same performance of reluctance and bargaining.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom reluctant at the fence as a new boy approaches with goods.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The barrel scene shows how the routine repeats for each newcomer.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bargaining goods are named visually.

image.subject: A busy stretch of whitewashed fence on a dusty street, several barefoot boys handing over kites, string, tickets and small glass bottles to each other in the afternoon sun.

storyboard.claim: Tom works tirelessly to sustain a functioning economy out of thin air.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boys trading goods along a busy fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The routine now shown as an active market.
storyboard.addedInformation: The economy is shown as busy and self-sustaining.

storyboard.claim: John Cely calls Tom an actor manager staging a production.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a quotation carries the beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A critic's reading of the performance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the critic's frame: Tom is a manager, not lazy.

image.subject: A small stack of hand-lettered paper tickets tied with string on a whitewashed fence rail, a boy's hand reaching to take one in the bright afternoon sun.

storyboard.claim: Tom literally printed his own currency in the form of tickets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stack of paper tickets on a fence rail.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The performance now becomes a currency.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tickets are the currency Tom invented.

storyboard.claim: This brings the argument back to its core thesis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a short bridge line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ties the currency back to the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the turn toward the general claim.

image.subject: A knot of townspeople in plain summer clothes talk together in a dusty street in small groups, heads leaning in, the heat shimmering above the boards.

storyboard.claim: Value is just a community agreement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townspeople gathered in small groups in the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thesis now gets a town-wide picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: The agreement is a crowd of people, not a single person.

image.subject: Four eager neighborhood boys stand along a whitewashed picket fence, one holding a paintbrush out to another, all of them looking keen and envious in the summer heat.

storyboard.claim: Tom convinces the town to value a punishment as a privilege.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boys eager to paint the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The agreement is shown in the eagerness of the boys.
storyboard.addedInformation: The punishment is now a sought-after privilege.

storyboard.claim: They agreed the fence was fun, so it became fun.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the statement carries the idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the agreement point with a short line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fun is shown as a shared decision.

image.subject: A dusty road in a small Missouri town on a summer morning, townsfolk in dark Sunday clothes walking toward a small plain wooden church.

storyboard.claim: Tom takes his newly acquired capital to the town's most rigid institution, the Sunday school.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townsfolk in Sunday clothes walking to church.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fence economy now moves toward the church.
storyboard.addedInformation: The setting shifts from fence to church.

image.subject: A Sunday school room with rows of wooden benches, a lectern with a Bible on it, bright windows and the faint smell of wax in the light.

storyboard.claim: The church is the next place to test the economy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Sunday school room with benches and a lectern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Enters the church the previous beat named.
storyboard.addedInformation: The room is the stage for the next sequence.

image.subject: A small, plain white wooden church in a Missouri river town with a pine-board box for a steeple on its roof, under a bright summer sky.

storyboard.claim: The Sunday school building is small, plain and austere.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Exterior of a plain wooden church with a box steeple.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The camera moves from the street to the building.
storyboard.addedInformation: The building's austerity sets up its rigid rules.

image.subject: Rows of hard, high-backed pine pews in a plain whitewashed church, empty and bare, with bright sun falling through a single window.

storyboard.claim: The church is a rigid, uncomfortable place built to make children suffer for their souls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Empty high-backed pine pews in a bare whitewashed church, sunlight on the bare boards.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the tour of the church begun in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The austere pews show the town's idea of discipline.

image.subject: A small stack of colored paper tickets, blue, red and yellow, laid out on a worn wooden table in a schoolroom.

storyboard.claim: The adults built a convoluted system of colored tickets to reward children for learning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three piles of blue, red and yellow paper tickets on a wooden table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pews lead into the ticket system.
storyboard.addedInformation: The three colors are the currency the rest of the chapter runs on.

image.subject: A sandy-haired boy in a grey cotton shirt stands by a Sunday school lectern, reciting from memory, and a blue paper ticket lies on the lectern beside him.

storyboard.claim: Memorizing two Bible verses earns one blue ticket.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy reciting at a lectern with one blue ticket on the wood.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ticket colors are now tied to a concrete task.
storyboard.addedInformation: The price of a blue ticket is two verses.

storyboard.claim: Ten tickets of each color trade up until ten yellow tickets buy a Bible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three text rows on the plain screen.
storyboard.onScreenText: 10 BLUE = 1 RED / 10 RED = 1 YELLOW / 10 YELLOW = 1 BIBLE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The single blue ticket now becomes a full ladder of exchange.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ten yellow tickets equal the thousands of memorized verses the Bible represents.

image.subject: A large heavy Bible with a gilt-edged cover resting on a polished parlor table, a lamp beside it, the room dim and respectable.

storyboard.claim: The superintendent awards a large Bible to whoever holds ten yellow tickets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heavy gilt-edged Bible on a polished table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ladder ends at this object.
storyboard.addedInformation: It is a heavy, impressive object, not an ordinary paperback.

image.subject: A large open illustrated Bible showing a dramatic engraving of a bearded prophet in a stormy landscape, the page heavy with dark ink.

storyboard.claim: The Bible is a large illustrated book with dramatic, detailed engravings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open page of a heavy illustrated Bible with a stormy engraving.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The prize Bible is now opened to show what it is.
storyboard.addedInformation: The engraving style is dramatic and dark, unlike a pocket Bible.

storyboard.claim: The engravings are almost terrifying biblical scenes, not gentle picture books.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on the screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the engraving on the open page.
storyboard.addedInformation: The illustrations are dark and dramatic.

storyboard.claim: The Bible is worth 40 cents, a significant sum for a child.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Large figure 40 cents on plain screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The explanation of the prize turns to its price.
storyboard.addedInformation: Forty cents is a real amount of money for a boy.

left.label: TICKETS
left.subject: A fist of colored paper tickets, earned one verse at a time by a child at a bench.

right.label: BIBLE
right.subject: A heavy gilt-edged Bible on a parlor table, the status object of a respectable family.

storyboard.claim: The Bible is the institution's ultimate reward, bought with tickets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two framed objects: a fist of tickets and a gilt Bible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The Bible prize is set against the currency that buys it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cost of the reward is the labor of memorizing.

image.subject: Rows of schoolchildren on wooden benches, each reciting from an open book, while a teacher's switch rests on a lectern at the front.

storyboard.claim: The economy relies on mind-numbing rote memorization.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Children on benches reciting from books in a sunlit classroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The Bible prize leads back to the work that earns it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scene shows the rote repetition the system depends on.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, slumped over a Bible on a bench, eyes drifting to the window.

storyboard.claim: Tom cannot memorize a single verse and has no patience for the work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom slumped over a Bible, staring at the window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rote work is now personal, and Tom is the one refusing it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's restlessness is the reason he will look for a shortcut.

image.subject: A scatter of black licorice sticks, bent fish hooks and white marbles laid out on a weathered plank fence.

storyboard.claim: Tom owns licorice, fish hooks and marbles that other boys want more than verses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Licorice, fish hooks and white marbles on a plank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's loot is the alternative currency he holds.
storyboard.addedInformation: These are the immediate-pleasure goods the tickets compete with.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue shirt and bare feet stands at the door of a whitewashed church with arms folded, a line of boys waiting on the dusty steps.

storyboard.claim: Tom waits at the church door before the service and intercepts the ticket economy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at the church door with a line of boys on the steps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The loot is now used at the door where the kids pass.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom positions himself as the gatekeeper of the currency.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer hands a stick of licorice to a round-faced boy in a grey shirt and frayed suspenders, who is eating an apple and holds out a blue ticket in exchange, on a dusty street outside a church.

storyboard.claim: Tom acts as a broker, trading licorice for other kids' tickets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom handing licorice to Ben Rogers for a blue ticket.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's loot becomes a trade.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ben Rogers is the boy who prefers a treat now to a promise later.

left.label: BIBLE
left.subject: An unopened heavy Bible on a table, a distant promise with dull pages.

right.label: LICORICE
right.subject: A stick of black licorice and a bent fish hook in a boy's palm, a pleasure he can hold now.

storyboard.claim: A distant promise of a Bible is less appealing than immediate licorice or a fish hook.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An unopened Bible set against licorice and a fish hook in a palm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The loot is compared with the prize.
storyboard.addedInformation: The immediate reward wins the boy's choice.

storyboard.claim: Tom skips the intellectual labor and buys the currency itself, the core of Twain's critique.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The broker trade is named as the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point is that the system can be gamed by buying the token.

image.subject: A row of gilt-edged prize cards and a polished brass medal set on a judge's table in a timber courtroom.

storyboard.claim: Society rewards the appearance of merit rather than real substance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gilt prize cards and a brass medal on a table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The Bible prize is generalized to all institutions.
storyboard.addedInformation: The prizes look like merit whether or not they were earned.

image.subject: A plain wooden ladder leaning against a whitewashed church wall in a dusty street, a few of its rungs painted gold.

storyboard.claim: Institutions reward the look of climbing rather than real ability.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wooden ladder with gold-painted rungs against a church wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The prize image becomes a climbing image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gold rungs show the appearance of advancement.

storyboard.claim: Any institutional reward system can be gamed by anyone who knows the currency and has the capital.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ladder is now a general rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Capital is what lets anyone game the system.

left.label: VIRTUE
left.subject: A grey-haired parson's hands folded over a Bible in prayer.

right.label: PURCHASING POWER
right.subject: A fistful of coins and colored tickets exchanged across a plank counter.

storyboard.claim: Adults think tickets stand for virtue, but they only stand for purchasing power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Folded hands over a Bible against coins and tickets on a counter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The institutional rule is now a choice between two meanings.
storyboard.addedInformation: The coins make the purchasing point literal.

storyboard.claim: Twain offers a tragic explicit contrast in the text.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Quotation card with no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leads into the German boy example.
storyboard.addedInformation: The contrast is the book's own, stated in the text.

image.subject: A sunlit Sunday school room with a single bench pulled up to a lectern, an open Bible on the stand and a worn slate of verses on the bench.

storyboard.claim: A boy of German parentage did the work exactly as the adults intended.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty bench and lectern in a sunlit classroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The contrast becomes a real person in the story.
storyboard.addedInformation: The empty bench shows where he worked.

storyboard.claim: The German boy memorized 3,000 verses without stopping.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Large figure 3,000 on plain screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bench is now a number.
storyboard.addedInformation: The number is the cost of the reward.

image.subject: A plain-coated man with a neutral, thoughtful face sits bowed at a desk in a dim room, his head in his hands, an unfinished slate beside him.

storyboard.claim: The mental strain left the boy little better than an idiot from that day forth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bowed figure at a desk, head in hands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The number of verses becomes a ruined mind.
storyboard.addedInformation: The figure stands in for the boy as an adult.

image.subject: A church platform with a lectern, a stiff superintendent in a black coat gesturing toward rows of seated townspeople in their Sunday best.

storyboard.claim: The superintendent loved to make the boy recite before company.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stiff superintendent on a platform before seated townspeople.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The strain is paired with the public display.
storyboard.addedInformation: The display is for the audience, not the boy.

image.subject: A quiet middle-aged man with a dark moustache in a dark suit and waistcoat, leaning on a writing desk with an open book, a half-smile.

storyboard.claim: The system destroyed the boy who followed the rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator leaning on a desk with an open book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narration pauses to name the indictment.
storyboard.addedInformation: The narrator speaks as the observer of the town.

storyboard.claim: Tom does not just expose the system; he conquers it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain question on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The indictment is challenged.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question reframes Tom's win as a victory.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue shirt stands on a church platform holding a fist of tickets, facing a stunned superintendent in a black coat.

storyboard.claim: Tom walks up with nine yellow and nine red tickets and demands the Bible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom holding tickets before a stunned superintendent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question is answered by Tom's demand.
storyboard.addedInformation: The superintendent's shock shows how unexpected the claim is.

left.label: TOM
left.subject: A freckled boy in a faded blue shirt sits on a church platform with a satisfied grin and a Bible on his knees.

right.label: THE GERMAN BOY
right.subject: A boy at a bench hunched over a stack of worn verse slips until late in the evening.

storyboard.claim: Tom gets the glory and the prize without the work the German boy did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom smiling with a Bible against a hunched boy with verse slips.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The German boy returns as the contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's prize is a shortcut to the same reward.

storyboard.claim: Tom wins the prize, but Twain asks whether he really wins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain question on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The glory is now questioned.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question sets up the cost of visibility.

image.subject: A freckled 12-year-old boy in a faded blue shirt sits beside a dignified man in a black frock coat and white high collar on a raised church platform, the congregation below them.

storyboard.claim: Tom sits beside Judge Thatcher, the most powerful man in town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom and the judge on a raised platform above the congregation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question of winning becomes a matter of status.
storyboard.addedInformation: The judge is the town's highest authority.

image.subject: A dignified man with grey side-whiskers and a black frock coat pats a freckled boy on the head, while a fair-haired girl in a pale blue dress with a ribbon watches from a pew.

storyboard.claim: The judge praises Tom as a fine, manly little fellow in front of Becky.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The judge's hand on Tom's head with Becky watching from a pew.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The platform praise becomes personal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Becky is watching, which is why Tom wants the status.

storyboard.claim: The judge asks Tom to name the first two disciples, a basic test of the scripture the reward claims to measure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain question on screen.
storyboard.onScreenText: TELL ME THE NAMES OF THE FIRST TWO DISCIPLES
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The praise is now tested.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question tests the reward against the work it was supposed to show.

image.subject: Colored paper tickets scattered across a church floor, blue, red and yellow, some lying under a pew.

storyboard.claim: The ticket economy crashes when the judge asks a real question.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tickets scattered across the floor under a pew.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question is answered by the collapse of the currency.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scattered tickets show the worth was never real.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired boy in a faded blue shirt stands flushed and tongue-tied on a church platform, one hand over his face, a stunned judge beside him.

storyboard.claim: Tom blurts out David and Goliath and is humiliated in front of the whole assembly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom flushed on the platform with his hand over his face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The collapse is now Tom's humiliation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wrong answer is what exposes the fraud.

image.subject: A fair-haired 11-year-old girl in a pale blue dress with a white pinafore and a ribbon in her hair, shy eyes and a careful posture, looking away from the front of a church.

storyboard.claim: Tom is humiliated in front of Becky, and the prize cannot protect him from the spotlight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Becky looking away with shy eyes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The humiliation is seen through Becky's eyes.
storyboard.addedInformation: The prize has not bought the respect he wanted.

storyboard.claim: Tom had the capital but no real product to back it up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The humiliation is named as impostor syndrome.
storyboard.addedInformation: Capital was the tickets; the product was the knowledge.

image.subject: Rows of townspeople packed on church pews, each holding up a colored paper ticket, nodding in agreement.

storyboard.claim: The town collectively agreed that colored tickets equaled holiness and theological knowledge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townspeople in pews holding up colored tickets.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The failure is the town's shared belief.
storyboard.addedInformation: The agreement is a crowd, not one person.

image.subject: A bent fish hook resting on a tin bucket beside a limp grey rat on a weathered plank, in the dusty light of a river town.

storyboard.claim: Tom bought the fake value system with a dead rat and a fish hook.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fish hook and a limp grey rat on a plank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The collective agreement is bought with trinkets.
storyboard.addedInformation: The objects show what the currency was worth.

storyboard.claim: The tickets meant absolutely nothing about Tom's real knowledge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bargain is now proven empty.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tickets did not reflect his knowledge.

image.subject: A close photograph of a small stack of colored Sunday school tickets on a worn wooden schoolroom desk in a Missouri town, one ticket lifted between two fingers in the window light.

storyboard.claim: The town agreed on the tickets as value, but the agreement is hollow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Colored Sunday school tickets on a desk, one held up for inspection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the thesis that value is a shared agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tickets are the currency the agreement rests on.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, a grin that is half mischief, a tin bucket in hand, standing beside a whitewashed picket fence on a dusty board sidewalk in summer.

storyboard.claim: Tom uses the same trick on the fence and in the Sunday school, and decides to scale it up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom beside a whitewashed fence with a tin bucket, scheming grin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the fence-and-tickets economy into a bigger plan.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the whitewash labour to the Sunday school currency.

storyboard.claim: Tom decides to manipulate the town's emotions and his own existence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only beat: the shock line lands on the words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates from tickets and fences to his own life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the funeral as Tom's own production.

storyboard.claim: The next sequence is one of the most famous and twisted in the book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only transition into the funeral sequence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A signpost before the story turns to the funeral.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the book's most famous set piece.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn, a thin barefoot 13-year-old in ragged homespun clothes with a battered straw hat, sitting on a rough wooden raft tied to a willow on the Mississippi bank at dusk, the broad brown river and an island of willows ahead.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck run away with a third boy to Jackson's Island to be pirates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two boys on a raft tied to a willow at dusk, the island ahead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the funeral framing to the escape that causes it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the island and the boys' pirate plan.

image.subject: An empty raft drifting on the broad brown Mississippi at dawn, a torn shirt snagged on its rope and no one aboard, the willows of the island on the far bank.

storyboard.claim: The town finds a runaway raft and assumes the boys drowned.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty raft drifting on the river, a torn shirt snagged on its rope.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys vanish; the town reads the empty raft as death.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows how the town reached its false conclusion.

storyboard.claim: The boys learn they are presumed drowned, and Tom sees an opportunity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only question on screen.
storyboard.onScreenText: And what does Tom do with that?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The raft finding turns into a question about Tom's next move.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the viewer ask what Tom will do with his own death.

image.subject: A white wooden church steeple in a small Missouri river town on a still Sunday morning, dew on the grass and a whitewashed picket fence in the foreground, the street empty.

storyboard.claim: A still Sabbath morning with the church bell tolling instead of ringing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A white church steeple on a silent morning, empty street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question of Tom's plan moves to the town's mourning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the solemn setting of the return.

image.subject: A stout grey-haired woman of about sixty in a black mourning dress and black veil, a grey-haired woman's hand on the arm of a neat 9-year-old boy in a pressed black suit, climbing the steps of a timber church in deep black.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly, Sid, Mary and the Harper family enter the church dressed in mourning black.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grieving aunt and a boy in black climbing church steps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The town's mourning families arrive after the tolling bell.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Aunt Polly in grief before the reveal of her suffering.

image.subject: A timber church interior in the 1840s, townspeople in dark clothes rising from their pews while a grieving family walks slowly down the aisle, heads bowed, sunlight from high windows.

storyboard.claim: The whole congregation rises as the grieving families walk down the aisle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A congregation standing as a family walks down the aisle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The families' arrival becomes a communal rising.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the town's collective grief as one picture.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, peering down through the balusters of a church gallery at the weeping congregation below, a grin tugging at his mouth.

storyboard.claim: Tom and his pirate brothers have secretly returned from the island and watch from the church gallery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom peering from the gallery rail at the weeping pews below.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mourners below are unaware that the dead boys are above them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the viewer in the gallery with Tom.

image.subject: A dim dusty church gallery loft stacked with broken old benches and forgotten furniture, two boys crouched low among them, a thin shaft of light from a small window on the floorboards.

storyboard.claim: The boys hide in a chaos of invalid benches and dusty furniture in the gallery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cluttered gallery loft with two crouched boys.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the hiding place a physical clutter.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the boys are hidden among junk, not seated in pews.

storyboard.claim: The boys are watching their own funeral, a masterpiece of dramatic irony.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the irony.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the gallery hiding into the irony of the scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the dramatic irony directly.

storyboard.claim: Society appreciates you most when you are entirely unavailable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the cynical truth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the irony to a general truth about people.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the thesis about social value and absence.

image.subject: Aunt Polly, a stout grey-haired woman of about sixty in a dark dress with a white collar and spectacles on a cord, dabbing her eyes with a handkerchief in a church pew, a black-clad congregation around her.

storyboard.claim: Community sentiment is manipulated by making someone seem gone for good.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly weeping in a pew with a handkerchief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The general truth now has a grieving face.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts Aunt Polly's grief on screen as the cost.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled sandy-haired 12-year-old boy, half-hidden in the shadows of a church gallery, a small satisfied grin on his face as he looks down at the town.

storyboard.claim: Tom discovers that his social stock rises as his value is measured by the town's grief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom in gallery shadow with a smug grin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the town's grief to Tom's own gain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom's satisfaction as a snapshot.

image.subject: A bare farmhouse kitchen wall with a hickory switch hung on a nail beside a stout woman's apron, a whitewash brush leaning on the floorboards below, morning light through the window.

storyboard.claim: Alive, Tom is a nuisance constantly whipped by Aunt Polly; dead, his value soars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A switch hanging on a kitchen wall, a whitewash brush on the floor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts Tom's life at home with his value as a ghost.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the switch that marked his life before the disappearance.

image.subject: A small weathered wooden grave marker at the edge of a churchyard, fresh turned earth beside it and a few wilted flowers, a sunlit church wall behind.

storyboard.claim: Dead, Tom becomes a hero, and the validation he gets from the rafters is insane.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fresh grave marker in a churchyard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The alive-versus-dead contrast becomes a grave.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the death staging literal with a grave marker.

image.subject: A minister in a black coat at a wooden lectern in a timber church, one arm lifted, a Bible open before him, preaching to a sobbing congregation in the afternoon light.

storyboard.claim: The minister reframes every mischievous act as evidence of noble spirit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A minister preaching at a lectern to a tearful congregation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The shared grief gets a voice in the sermon.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the sermon as the town's reframing of the boys.

image.subject: A row of townspeople in dark clothes in a timber church, handkerchiefs at their eyes, all singing from open hymnals, faces lifted toward the rafters.

storyboard.claim: The congregation is sobbing as the minister calls for a hymn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sobbing townspeople singing from hymnals.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sermon leads into the singing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the hymn being sung by the mourners.

storyboard.claim: Old Hundred is a classic somber doxology hymn and a crucial detail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only naming of the hymn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the hymn the congregation is about to sing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies the hymn as a funeral doxology.

storyboard.claim: The hymn text praises God from whom all blessings flow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only quotation of the doxology line.
storyboard.onScreenText: Praise God from whom all blessings flow
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hymn's name is followed by its words.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the actual hymn lyric as a quotation.

image.subject: An open worn hymnal on a wooden lectern in a 19th-century Calvinist church, candlelight on its yellowed pages and the empty pews beyond.

storyboard.claim: Singing this hymn at a funeral seals the boys' permanence in the community's story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open hymnal on a lectern in candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sung hymn becomes an object of finality.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the hymn as a sealed record.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn crouched in a dusty church gallery, Huck, a thin barefoot boy in a battered straw hat, staring down with an envious and watchful look while Tom turns to him, the hymn swelling below.

storyboard.claim: As the hymn swells, Tom looks at his envious friends Huck and Joe from the hiding spot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom and Huck in the gallery, Huck envious.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hymn's climax shifts the focus to the boys.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the friends who envy Tom's position.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, arms folded and chin up in the church gallery shadows, a window's light on his proud face.

storyboard.claim: Tom confesses in his heart that this is the proudest moment of his life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom with folded arms and proud face in gallery shadow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the envious friends to Tom's own pride.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom's inner satisfaction as a physical posture.

image.subject: Sunlight across a timber church pew in which mourners sit weeping in black, and on the wall behind them the shadow of a boy leaning over the gallery rail.

storyboard.claim: Tom is soaking in the worship of the town, consuming its grief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sunlit weeping pew with a boy's shadow on the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pride becomes a consumption of the town's sorrow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the grief as something Tom feeds on.

storyboard.claim: It is pure ego; Tom has achieved peak social value.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only punchline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the gallery sequence with a verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the moral verdict on Tom's ego.

image.subject: A quiet middle-aged man with a dark moustache in a dark suit and waistcoat, leaning on a writing desk with an open book, a half-smile on his face, the light of a window on the page.

storyboard.claim: It is hard to see the genius of the scheme while the morality of it disguises the view.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator at a writing desk with an open book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The analysis turns to a critical voice, and the narrator's desk frames it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Recalls the trading and gaming of the earlier chapters.

image.subject: Aunt Polly, a stout grey-haired woman in a black mourning dress with a white collar, alone in a dim kitchen with one hand pressed to her face and her spectacles in the other hand.

storyboard.claim: This crosses a serious line; Aunt Polly is genuinely suffering.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly alone in a dim kitchen, hand to her face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The analysis now has a face of the suffering.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows her grief outside the church.

image.subject: A bedroom at night lit by one tallow candle, a stout grey-haired woman kneeling beside an empty bed with a patched quilt, her head bowed over her clasped hands.

storyboard.claim: Earlier, Aunt Polly wept by Tom's bed, believing he was dead, saying she had broken his heart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly kneeling beside an empty bed in candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The suffering is confirmed by an earlier scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the earlier grief at the bedside.

storyboard.claim: To let an old woman who loves you weep in a black dress just to feed your ego is not a childish prank.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the moral cost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The earlier grief is now a moral charge.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the act as a harm, not a prank.

image.subject: A black-gloved hand gripping a folded handkerchief on the rail of a timber church pew, the wood worn smooth and a single window's light across it.

storyboard.claim: Twain does not shy away from the immense pain this causes, and the act is borderline sociopathic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A black-gloved hand gripping a handkerchief on a pew rail.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The moral judgment is given a physical sign of grief.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pain as a gesture in place of gore.

image.subject: An empty wooden stage in a small riverside hall at dusk, a painted canvas backdrop of a forest, and a single candle in a tin lantern set on the boards.

storyboard.claim: To understand Tom, the actor-manager lens is needed: Tom as director of his own show.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty stage with a painted forest backdrop and one lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The moral judgment is reframed through theatre.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the stage metaphor.

storyboard.claim: To Tom it is theater, not malice: a play requires an audience and a tragedy requires tears.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only quotation of the theatre line.
storyboard.onScreenText: A play requires an audience. A tragedy requires tears.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stage metaphor becomes an explicit argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the logic of Tom's theatre.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, clinging to a single floating log on the dark brown Mississippi at dusk, his face set and determined.

storyboard.claim: Tom is so committed to the bit that he risked his life to make his return happen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom clinging to a single log on the dark river at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The theatre commitment is shown as physical risk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the crossing that the next beat explains.

image.subject: The wide dangerous Missouri shore at dusk, a single log drifting in dark water, the far bank a thin dark line and a steamboat's smoke on the horizon.

storyboard.claim: He paddled across the massive dangerous river on a single log at dusk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A single log drifting on a dark river at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The log from the last beat is set in its wide river.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the scale of the crossing.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, crouched behind the trunk of a tree in a dark wood at night, peering toward the lit window of a farmhouse.

storyboard.claim: Tom sneaks through the woods to secure his front-row seat to his own myth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom crouched behind a tree, peering at a lit window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The crossing leads to the sneaking through the woods.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom watching the household as an audience.

storyboard.claim: Tom is the director, and the town does not know it is in a play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the director idea.
storyboard.onScreenText: THEY DON'T KNOW THEY'RE IN THE PLAY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stage metaphor is named as direction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the play to the thesis about value.

image.subject: A crowd of townspeople in dark clothes gathered on the dusty street outside a timber church in the sunlight, all turned toward the steps, nodding in agreement with one another.

storyboard.claim: Tom forced the whole town to publicly agree on his irreplaceable worth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A crowd of townspeople outside a church, all nodding.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thesis returns with the whole town in agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the public agreement as a crowd.

image.subject: A sand-filled hourglass on a wooden windowsill with its last grains falling, the light of a dusky window across it and an empty room behind.

storyboard.claim: Tom manufactured the ultimate scarcity, death, to drive his value through the roof.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass with the last grains falling on a windowsill.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thesis closes on the image of scarcity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the scarcity of death a time-based symbol.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, a grin that is half mischief, a tin bucket in hand, standing on a dusty St. Petersburg street at sunset with a whitewashed picket fence behind him.

storyboard.claim: Tom's theatrical world, where he controls every variable, is about to hit reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom with his bucket on a dusty street at sunset, the confident grin still on his face.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE PLAY ENDS / STAGE MANAGE / ROBIN HOOD
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the spin-economy close of the last chunk; now the play is ending.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom is still in full control of his own fantasy at this point.

image.subject: The timber steps of the county courthouse in St. Petersburg at dusk, a knot of grave townspeople in dark 1840s coats and bonnets standing in the fading light.

storyboard.claim: The play economy is about to shatter against the adult world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The courthouse steps at dusk with serious townspeople gathered.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's make-believe is contrasted with the sober adult town.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the adult institutions that will judge the boys' secret.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn stand at the gate of a dark graveyard at midnight, a lantern-less road stretching back toward distant town lights, a dead cat tied in a rag hanging from Huck's hand.

storyboard.claim: The boys are a mile and a half from town at a graveyard at midnight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two boys at a dark graveyard gate, a dead cat in a rag, distant town lights.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The Halloween play moves from the street to the graveyard.
storyboard.addedInformation: Distance from town signals isolation.

image.subject: A crazy board fence leaning inward at a graveyard edge, round-topped boards gnawed by weather, staggering over sunken grave mounds in pitch darkness lit only by a thin moon.

storyboard.claim: The graveyard is pitch black with a fence leaning inward over sunken graves.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A leaning board fence over sunken mounds under a thin moon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the approach to the graveyard.
storyboard.addedInformation: Decay and unease in the setting.

image.subject: Two boys crouched close together behind a leaning tombstone in a dark graveyard, a dead elm bending in the wind above them, the wind moaning through its branches.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck are huddled and terrified in the graveyard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two crouched boys behind a tombstone under a bending dead elm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fear builds from the fence to the boys themselves.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wind and the dead elm supply the eerie mood.

image.subject: A dead grey tabby cat lying on a flat grave slab under moonlight in an old graveyard, a rag and a short cord beside it, the superstition of a midnight cure.

storyboard.claim: They have a dead cat and are trying to cure warts with a childhood superstition.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dead cat on a grave slab in moonlight with a rag and cord beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys' midnight errand is explained.
storyboard.addedInformation: The superstition is shown as a literal prop.

image.subject: Three dim figures approaching along a graveyard path through the gloom, one of them swinging an old-fashioned tin lantern whose light trembles over leaning wooden grave markers, seen from behind a clump of brush.

storyboard.claim: Voices and vague figures approach, swinging a tin lantern.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three dim figures on a graveyard path, one with a swinging tin lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys' hiding turns into the moment of hearing voices.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lantern is the only light and the first clue of approaching men.

storyboard.claim: The boys think it is devils or the ghost of Hos Williams.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card asking whether they are devils or a ghost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lantern's light spreads on the ground, so the boys assume the supernatural.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the boys' superstition as a question.

image.subject: A pair of bare boy's feet in the dirt at the edge of a lantern's circle of light, poised to bolt into the dark brush, a tangle of weeds behind them.

storyboard.claim: Childhood fantasy meets harsh adult reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bare feet at the lantern's edge, poised to run.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The voices turn fear into the moment of collision.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the boys' childhood to the adult danger.

left.label: THE PLAY
left.subject: A barefoot boy in a homemade paper hat waving a stick like a sword on a sunny dusty street, grinning at an audience of other boys.

right.label: THE TOWN
right.subject: Townspeople in black Sunday clothes gathered at a white church door in the summer sun, sombre and unconvinced.

storyboard.claim: Tom has conned his way out of chores and staged his own funeral; he is master of the play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy playing a sword game against a sombre Sunday crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The earlier fantasy is set against the adult town.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's spin is contrasted with the town's grave reality.

image.subject: A rusted clasp knife and a lead musket ball lying on a rough plank table in a dim room, a single tallow candle burning beside them.

storyboard.claim: You cannot negotiate with a bullet or a knife.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A knife and a musket ball on a table beside a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fantasy has no power against real weapons.
storyboard.addedInformation: Real danger replaces the play economy's negotiation.

image.subject: A thin, barefoot 13-year-old boy in ragged homespun clothes, a battered straw hat with a torn brim, dirt on his face and a sly, watchful expression, crouched in brush and peering through leaves with widening eyes.

storyboard.claim: Huck recognizes the voices, so the fantasy shatters instantly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Huck crouched in brush, eyes widening in recognition.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The approaching figures are about to be named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Huck's recognition is the turn from fear to certainty.

image.subject: Three men on a dusk graveyard path: a ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and a torn grey shirt, a young doctor in a dark frock coat carrying a leather bag, and a gaunt dark-haired man in a torn brown coat and slouch hat with a cold, unblinking stare.

storyboard.claim: The figures are Muff Potter, young Dr. Robinson and Injun Joe, real humans not devils.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three named adults on a graveyard path at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lantern figures are revealed as people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the three adults and their roles.

image.subject: A fresh mound of dark earth beside an open grave at midnight, a spade stuck upright in the dirt, a lantern set on the grass beside a leaning wooden marker.

storyboard.claim: A respected town doctor is robbing a grave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spade in fresh earth beside an open grave at midnight.
