storyboard.relationToPrevious: The voices turn out to be grave robbers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the grave robbery without showing the body.

image.subject: An 1840s physician's study with leather-bound anatomy books on a shelf, a bare skeleton on a wooden stand and a single candle burning on a writing desk.

storyboard.claim: Medical science advanced, but the legal supply of cadavers was almost nonexistent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An 1840s anatomy study with books and a skeleton.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The grave robbery is now explained by medical need.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why doctors needed bodies.

image.subject: A shadowy man in a long coat counting silver coins into the palm of a grave-digger beside a wooden picket fence at night, a lantern on the ground between them.

storyboard.claim: Doctors paid resurrection men, grave robbers, to dig up fresh bodies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Coins passed to a grave-digger beside a fence at night.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The anatomy need becomes a payment.
storyboard.addedInformation: The underground trade is shown as a bargain.

image.subject: An open pine coffin lid leaning against a wooden picket fence in a churchyard at dawn, a shovel stuck in the turned earth beside it.

storyboard.claim: Grave robbers dig up freshly buried bodies to study anatomy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A coffin lid leaning on a fence beside a shovel in turned earth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the economy of the grave trade.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the aftermath of a dig, not the body.

image.subject: A worn ledger open on a counting table, a pile of coins beside a pair of calloused hands, a candle guttering in a dim back room.

storyboard.claim: The underground economy is driven by greed and desperation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ledger, coins and calloused hands in a dim room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payment is now framed as an economy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Greed and desperation are shown through money and hands.

left.label: MUFF DEMANDS
left.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard, torn grey shirt, holding out an open hand and demanding more money in a dim alley.

right.label: DOCTOR REFUSES
right.subject: A young doctor in a dark frock coat turning away with a stern face, one hand gripping a heavy wooden plank in the lantern light.

storyboard.claim: A fight over money breaks out between Muff Potter and the doctor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A demanding man and a refusing doctor, with the doctor holding a plank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The grave-robbing economy turns into a quarrel.
storyboard.addedInformation: The argument over money is the spark.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat, a hard face with a scar and an unshaven jaw, half-hidden behind a leaning tombstone, a blade catching the lantern light in his hand.

storyboard.claim: Injun Joe, with a long-standing grudge against the doctor's family, jumps in with a knife.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe behind a tombstone with a blade catching lantern light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The argument moves toward the knife.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grudge is shown as Joe's stance and his weapon.

image.subject: A dark empty graveyard at midnight, a lantern lying on its side in the grass beside an open grave, a dropped slouch hat on the ground and a leaning wooden marker in the moonlight.

storyboard.claim: Injun Joe commits cold-blooded murder in front of the boys.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty graveyard at midnight with a fallen lantern and a dropped hat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The knife has been raised; the scene is shown as aftermath.
storyboard.addedInformation: The violence is shown through its traces, not its act.

left.label: SUNDAY SCHOOL
left.subject: Children in a bright Sunday school room trading small paper tickets across rows of wooden benches, sunlight through the windows.

right.label: MIDNIGHT
right.subject: A dark graveyard of leaning wooden markers at midnight, lit only by a lantern held low in the grass.

storyboard.claim: The tone whiplashes from church tickets to a midnight murder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bright Sunday school beside a dark midnight graveyard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The murder scene is set against the earlier church world.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shock is shown through the two worlds.

storyboard.claim: Does Twain lose control of the tone with a penny dreadful murder?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card on whether the tone breaks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tonal whiplash is now a question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the argument that the jarring tone is intentional.

image.subject: A whitewashed picket fence in bright summer sun, the paint peeling in long strips to reveal grey weathered wood beneath, a dusty St. Petersburg street beyond.

storyboard.claim: Twain intentionally rips the mask off St. Petersburg.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A whitewashed fence peeling to grey wood.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question of tone is answered with a metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The whitewash veneer is literally shown peeling.

storyboard.claim: Violent frontier reality simmers beneath the polite whitewash veneer of the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A place card naming St. Petersburg with the frontier beneath.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The peeling fence becomes the town's naming.
storyboard.addedInformation: The town is named as the place hiding violence.

left.label: TOM'S OUTLAW
left.subject: A freckled boy in a paper pirate hat holding a wooden sword, grinning on a sunny street.

right.label: ENGINE JOE
right.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in a torn brown coat and slouch hat, a scar on his face, staring coldly from a dark doorway.

storyboard.claim: Tom wants to be a pirate or Robin Hood, but Injun Joe is what a real outlaw looks like.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy with a paper pirate hat beside a scarred, cold-eyed man in a slouch hat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The murder is now set against Tom's fantasy of outlaws.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's version of an outlaw is set against the real one.

image.subject: A child's cloth mask and a torn white sheet lying in a dirt road beneath a bare tree at dusk, the costumes of pretending abandoned in the dust.

storyboard.claim: The Halloween spooks are real world consequences of adult greed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cloth mask and torn sheet in a dusty road at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's costumes and games are now left behind.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask and sheet stand for the abandoned play.

image.subject: Two barefoot boys running down a dark dirt road away from a graveyard, silhouetted against a low moon, their shapes small against the long road.

storyboard.claim: The ultimate reality check: the boys run for their lives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two running silhouettes on a dark road under a low moon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The murder leads straight to flight.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the boys' reaction as flight.

image.subject: A rough pine shingle lying on a splintered bench in a dim old tannery, a bent pin beside it and a small dark red stain on the wood, hides and tanning vats in the shadows behind.

storyboard.claim: They make a blood oath to keep silent, writing it on a pine shingle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A pine shingle and a bent pin on a bench in a tannery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The flight ends at the tannery.
storyboard.addedInformation: The oath is shown as a prop.

image.subject: Two boys' hands pressed palm to palm over a pine shingle on a tannery bench, the wood's grain and dim light around them.

storyboard.claim: The boys swear they will drop dead if they tell.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two palms pressed together over the shingle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The blood oath becomes a physical pact.
storyboard.addedInformation: The silence pact is shown as a gesture.

storyboard.claim: Even in the face of horror, there is a community agreement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A statement card about the agreement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The oath is named as an agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the oath back to the book's theme.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck value their own safety over telling the truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A statement card on safety over truth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pact is named as a choice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The moral choice is stated plainly.

image.subject: A crowd of townspeople in dull Sunday clothes gathered at a graveyard gate at dawn, one man pointing down the road with a hand, the group turned toward the town.

storyboard.claim: The town wakes, finds the body and needs someone to blame.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townspeople at a graveyard gate at dawn, one pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The silence leads to the search for blame.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the town hunting for a scapegoat.

image.subject: A small isolated framed jail of unpainted timber on a dusty town lane, a single barred window, two barefoot boys lingering by a picket fence nearby.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck hang around the small isolated framed jail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A timber jail on a dusty lane with two boys by a fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Blame lands on Muff Potter, and the boys go to the jail.
storyboard.addedInformation: The jail is introduced as the place of the innocent man.

image.subject: Two boys' hands pushing a twist of tobacco and a box of matches through the iron bars of a jail window at night, a chain hanging on the wall inside.

storyboard.claim: Consumed with guilt, the boys hand Muff Potter tobacco and matches through the bars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two small hands passing tobacco and matches through iron bars.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The jail is now the place of guilt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gifts show the boys' guilt.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, torn grey shirt and stained trousers, sitting on the floor of a jail cell, chained at the wrist, reaching through the bars toward the light.

storyboard.claim: Muff Potter is chained on the ground floor, waiting to be hanged for a murder he did not commit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff Potter chained on a cell floor reaching toward the bars.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The gifts reach the chained man.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains show the innocent man's captivity.

image.subject: A large grizzled hand stopped at the iron bars of a jail window, the small hands of two boys on the other side, the gap too narrow for the big hand to pass through.

storyboard.claim: Muff notes that his hands are too big to fit through the bars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A big hand against the bars with two small hands outside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The gift is now blocked by the bars.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bars make the size of the hand visible.

storyboard.claim: Muff Potter says, Little hands and weak.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quotation card from Muff Potter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bars continue the scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Muff's words are quoted directly.

storyboard.claim: The boys have helped Muff Potter a little, and would help him more if they could.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A statement card on the boys' small help.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Muff's quote is answered with a statement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boys' limited help is named.

image.subject: An empty courthouse bench in dim light, a single bar of sunlight across the floorboards and a closed Bible on the railing, the room silent.

storyboard.claim: The lesson is the crushing moral cost of silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty courtroom bench in a bar of light with a closed Bible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The jail and guilt lead to the courtroom silence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Silence is shown as the empty room.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet peeks out from behind a half-open timber door in a dim 1840s hallway, one eye visible, a guilty look on his face.

storyboard.claim: Tom protects himself by hiding from the moral problem rather than facing it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom peeking from behind a door, half hidden.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the courtroom-of-conscience thread from the previous explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The image shows the act of hiding, which the words describe abstractly.

image.subject: A tin bucket tipped over on a dusty board sidewalk of a small Missouri river town in summer, a whitewashed picket fence beside it with one broken board, heat-shimmer in the air.

storyboard.claim: Opting out of responsibility causes damage that spreads to others.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abandoned tin bucket and broken fence on a dusty street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the hiding idea into a visible consequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fallen bucket and broken fence show what is left behind when someone steps away.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, wearing a torn grey shirt and stained trousers, chained at the wrist, sitting alone on a plank cot in a small stone jail cell.

storyboard.claim: The most vulnerable person in the room pays for others' silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff Potter chained on a cot in a cell.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the person who pays the price.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chain at his wrist shows he is held, not free.

storyboard.claim: Someone else, usually the most vulnerable, ends up paying the price.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Quotation card on plain background.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the general rule after the example of the jail.
storyboard.addedInformation: A general principle worth reading slowly.

image.subject: A knot of respectable townspeople in dark 1840s coats and bonnets stand on a board sidewalk in St. Petersburg, Missouri, heads turned toward a small stone jail at the end of the street.

storyboard.claim: The respectable citizens prefer an easy scapegoat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townspeople looking toward the jail.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the principle to the town that applies it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crowd's gaze points at the jail, which shows whom they blame.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat, a hard face with a scar and an unshaven jaw, walking along a dusty town street with his hands in his coat pockets, not looking at anyone.

storyboard.claim: The lethal predator walks freely among the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe walking a town street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the true threat the town ignores.
storyboard.addedInformation: He moves openly through the street, which shows his freedom.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat with a neutral, thoughtful expression stands among a small crowd of townspeople on a courthouse step, nodding along to what the others are saying.

storyboard.claim: The community agrees on Muff's guilt because it is psychologically convenient.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grey-coated townsman nodding in a crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the townspeople agreeing with the scapegoat story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Everyman stands for the ordinary citizen who goes along.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, wearing a torn grey shirt and chained at the wrist, grips the bars of a jail window and looks out with a grateful, teary expression.

storyboard.claim: Muff pours out gratitude for the boys' small kindness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff gripping jail bars, grateful.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the man whose gratitude the boys receive.
storyboard.addedInformation: His grip on the bars shows how much the gift matters to him.

storyboard.claim: Muff thanks the boys for memories of kindness they repay with silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-item list of what Muff recalls.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists what the boys once gave him.
storyboard.addedInformation: The list is the favour Muff remembers, which makes the silence worse.

storyboard.claim: Loyalty becomes complicity when it holds a man in chains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Question card, text only.
storyboard.onScreenText: Is loyalty still loyalty when it keeps a man in chains?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns Muff's thanks into a real question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question asks the viewer to judge the boys' silence.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet stands outside a small stone jail window, looking in at a chained man, his grin gone.

storyboard.claim: Tom visits the jail and cannot bring himself to speak.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom outside the jail window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts Tom at the scene of his silence.
storyboard.addedInformation: He stands outside the bars, which shows he is free while Muff is not.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt sits on a whitewashed picket fence with his back to a jail, head bowed, hands clasped between his knees, a dusty street in summer light.

storyboard.claim: Tom turns away from the truth he knows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sitting on a fence with his back turned.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Tom's choice to look away.
storyboard.addedInformation: His bowed head and turned back show the choice to stay silent.

image.subject: A heavy timber jail door in a small stone building, an iron chain and padlock hanging across it in the afternoon light, a dusty street in front.

storyboard.claim: The town prepares to execute an innocent man in chains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chained jail door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the jail that holds the innocent man.
storyboard.addedInformation: The padlock and chain make the wait visible.

image.subject: A quiet middle-aged man with a dark moustache in a dark suit and waistcoat leans on a writing desk with an open book, a half-smile, a lamp on the desk, looking up as if reflecting.

storyboard.claim: It is easy to judge Tom from a safe modern seat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator at a desk with an open book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the narrator in to step back from the judgment.
storyboard.addedInformation: The narrator's safe, seated pose matches the distance the claim describes.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat stands in the shadow of a courthouse porch, a hard face with a scar, his cold, unblinking stare aimed at the viewer.

storyboard.claim: A boy believes the lethal man will kill him if he speaks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe in a porch shadow, staring.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the threat that makes Tom afraid.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cold stare shows why a boy would fear him.

image.subject: A lone man in a slouch hat walks a dusty town street at dusk past whitewashed picket fences, his shadow long in the low sun, the houses shut tight.

storyboard.claim: The killer walks free through town, and a boy fears what he might do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lone figure on a dusk street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the threat moving through town.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shut houses and long shadow show the town's unease.

image.subject: Two boys, one a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old in a faded blue shirt and the other a thin, barefoot 13-year-old in ragged homespun clothes with a battered straw hat, clasp hands under a willow tree by a muddy river bank at dusk.

storyboard.claim: Tom's silence is a clash between a childhood oath and a developing conscience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom and Huck clasping hands under a willow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the oath that binds Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clasped hands show the childhood vow as a physical bond.

image.subject: A dim graveyard at midnight with leaning wooden markers, a dead elm tree silhouetted against moonlight through leaves, lit only by a single lantern on the ground.

storyboard.claim: Tom's dreams are infested with the horrors of the graveyard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A midnight graveyard with a lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the oath to the memory that haunts Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dead elm and leaning markers recall the murder scene.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt sits up in a narrow bed in a dark bedroom, a single tallow candle on a small table beside him, his face pale and drawn, staring into the dark.

storyboard.claim: Tom is physically deteriorating from the secret.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sitting up in bed by a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the cost of the secret on Tom's body.
storyboard.addedInformation: The candle and wakeful pose show sleepless nights.

storyboard.claim: The town has agreed on a false narrative built on Injun Joe's lie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.onScreenText: A false story, agreed by the whole town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the trap that Tom is caught in.
storyboard.addedInformation: The town agreed to it, which is the point.

image.subject: A small pile of gold coins on a rough wooden table beside a tallow candle, the candle's light catching the metal, in a dim 1840s room.

storyboard.claim: Tom holds the truth of the murder as a valuable currency.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gold coins beside a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the truth into a valuable thing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gold coins make the truth into currency that can be spent.

image.subject: A narrow limestone cave passage with dripping stone walls, a single candle flame held in a boy's hand casting small light, the walls closing in around him.

storyboard.claim: Spending the truth might cost Tom his life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A candle in a cave passage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the danger of using what he holds.
storyboard.addedInformation: The closing walls show the risk of acting.

image.subject: A crowded timber courtroom packed with townspeople on hard benches, a raised judge's bench at the front and a single window of light falling across the packed rows.

storyboard.claim: The courthouse is packed to the rafters for the trial.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A packed courtroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the reader into the courtroom for the trial.
storyboard.addedInformation: The packed benches show the town's appetite for spectacle.

storyboard.claim: The trial is the biggest entertainment in town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-item list of who attends.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds who is in the crowd.
storyboard.addedInformation: Both sexes and all ages attend, which shows the scale.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard, pale and haggard, in a torn grey shirt with chains on his wrists, seated at the defendant's bench in a timber courtroom.

storyboard.claim: Potter sits pale and hopeless in chains before the court.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff seated in chains at the defendant's bench.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the accused man in the courtroom.
storyboard.addedInformation: His pale, hopeless face shows what the trial means to him.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat sits still on a courtroom bench, a hard face with a scar, showing no emotion at all, eyes fixed forward.

storyboard.claim: Injun Joe sits completely calm in the courtroom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe seated, expressionless.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Places the killer in the same room as the accused.
storyboard.addedInformation: His calm stillness is the menace.

image.subject: A dignified man in his fifties in a black frock coat and white high collar, grey side-whiskers, taking his seat on a raised bench in a timber courtroom, a gavel on the bench before him.

storyboard.claim: The judge arrives to preside with grave order.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Judge Thatcher taking his seat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the authority of the court.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bench and gavel show the law taking its seat.

storyboard.claim: The prosecution lays out an ironclad case against Muff.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Place card for the courtroom, text only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets out the case against the accused.
storyboard.addedInformation: The case is presented as airtight, which the town believes.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat with a neutral, thoughtful expression stands among a tense courtroom crowd, looking toward the defence table as a lawyer rises to speak.

storyboard.claim: Everyone assumes Muff is doomed until the defence speaks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grey-coated townsman in a tense courtroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the room's certainty before the turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crowd's expectant faces show the settled verdict.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet stands at the witness stand in a timber courtroom, breathless, his hand gripping the rail.

storyboard.claim: Tom is called to the stand and is breathless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at the witness stand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts Tom on the stand after the defence calls him.
storyboard.addedInformation: His gripping hand shows his fear.

left.label: TOM
left.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt standing at the witness stand, his mouth open, no words coming.

right.label: INJUN JOE
right.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in a torn brown coat and slouch hat, staring back coldly across the courtroom.

storyboard.claim: Tom stares at Injun Joe and his tongue fails him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom and Injun Joe facing each other across the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the boy and killer face to face.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two faces show the stakes of the moment.

storyboard.claim: True heroism means risking your own capital, not other people's.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.onScreenText: Risking your own capital, not someone else's.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the moment into the book's central idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: The contrast with trading chores and tickets is explicit.

storyboard.claim: True heroism requires risking your own physical safety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Quotation card on plain background.
storyboard.onScreenText: "True heroism requires risking your own safety."
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the principle from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bar is set high on purpose.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt stands in a shaft of window light in a timber courtroom, one hand raised as he speaks, having stepped out from the crowd.

storyboard.claim: Tom steps out from behind his stagecraft to face real consequences.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom standing in window light, speaking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Tom now standing in the open.
storyboard.addedInformation: The window light sets him apart from the crowd.

image.subject: A courtroom audience of townspeople in 1840s dress, faces turned intently toward a boy standing in the light, mouths slightly open, hanging on his every word.

storyboard.claim: Every eye is fixed on Tom as he warms to his subject.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Rapt courtroom faces turned toward Tom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the audience captured by Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: Their faces show Tom has the room.

storyboard.claim: Tom weaves a spell and loses track of time, as he did with the boys.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.onScreenText: Weaving a spell, taking no note of time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects Tom's courtroom talk to his storytelling with the boys.
storyboard.addedInformation: The link to the earlier storytelling makes the point.

image.subject: An empty courtroom aisle with a toppled wooden bench and scattered papers on the floor, dust hanging in a shaft of light from a tall window, the room in disarray.

storyboard.claim: The climax erupts in the courtroom as the accused falls and the killer springs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A toppled bench in a courtroom aisle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the aftermath of the climax without violence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The disorder shows the chaos without depicting harm.

image.subject: An open courtroom window with a white curtain blowing inward, and beyond it a dark figure in a slouch hat running across a grassy yard away from the building.

storyboard.claim: The killer escapes through a window, and is gone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open window and a fleeing figure beyond.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the escape after the climax.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blowing curtain and running figure make the escape visible.

image.subject: The broad brown Mississippi at dusk, a steamboat's smoke on the horizon beyond a willow-lined shore, a raft tied to a willow in the foreground.

storyboard.claim: Tom breaks the community agreement and shatters the false story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The river at dusk with a steamboat on the horizon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the open river where the truth now flows.
storyboard.addedInformation: The river and steamboat suggest the story moving beyond the town.

storyboard.claim: If Tom risks his life to save an innocent man, is he finally a classic good boy?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Question card, text only.
storyboard.onScreenText: Is Tom finally the classic good boy?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the courtroom act into a judgment about Tom.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question sets up the Horatio Alger reading that follows.

image.subject: A quiet middle-aged man with a dark moustache in a dark suit and waistcoat, leaning on a writing desk in a book-lined study, an open book in front of him and a half-smile on his face.

storyboard.claim: The reading of Tom as a Horatio Alger hero is a tempting but flat story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator at his desk, dry half-smile, weighing a cheap moral tale.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the discussion after the trial, pulling the frame back to the reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: Alger's rags-to-riches stories were popular in 1840s America.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, standing in a timber courtroom with townspeople turning to look at him, his face tight with resolve.

storyboard.claim: Tom faced his fears, told the truth and saved Muff.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom standing alone in the courtroom, townspeople watching.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the coming-of-age reading just voiced.
storyboard.addedInformation: The courtroom is the same timber room where the town convicted Muff.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat sitting in a parlour armchair, reading a cheap paperback novel with a neutral, thoughtful expression, a clock on the mantel behind him.

storyboard.claim: It is tempting to read the story as a standard redemption arc.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reader in a parlour finishing a cheap tale and nodding along.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Alger thread: the reader is the one who wants the neat ending.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dime novels were cheap serial fiction sold to the public.

storyboard.claim: Why did Tom step forward at all?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only question card; the shape of the question is the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the argument to motive.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question card frames motive as the open puzzle of the chapter.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, standing at the door of a lawyer's house at midnight, a lantern held low, his face pale and drawn.

storyboard.claim: Tom went to the lawyer in the dead of night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at a dark doorstep with a lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the why: the conscience drove him out.
storyboard.addedInformation: The night before the trial, the lawyer's house is a dark, quiet street.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, sitting up in a narrow bed in a dim bedroom with a candle guttering on a nightstand, eyes wide open.

storyboard.claim: Anxiety, not a wish to be respectable, pushed Tom into the adult world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sleepless in bed by candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the pressure a body.
storyboard.addedInformation: Candlelight over a sleepless bed shows the anxiety that drives him.

storyboard.claim: He did not want to be a hero; he wanted the nightmares to stop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement, banter between the two speakers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the bed image with the emotional point.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two speakers in banter show fear, not heroism, as the real motive.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, sitting on a hard courtroom bench with his head bowed and his hands clasped tight.

storyboard.claim: Tom did not cheerfully join the system; he was crushed into compliance by his own conscience.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom on a courtroom bench, head bowed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the agreement that he joined willingly.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom bowed on the bench shows conscience crushing him into the system.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, wearing a torn grey shirt and stained trousers, chained at the wrist, standing before a crowded timber courtroom of townspeople on hard benches.

storyboard.claim: The town agreed Muff was guilty, and Tom used the truth to undo that agreement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff chained in a packed courtroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from Tom's conscience to the town's verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: Muff is the innocent man the town convicted.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat, a hard face with a scar, an unshaven jaw and a cold, unblinking stare, seated among townspeople in a courtroom.

storyboard.claim: Tom used the truth to bankrupt Injun Joe's lie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe in the courtroom, cold stare.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the liar whose story Tom broke.
storyboard.addedInformation: Injun Joe's cold stare in court shows the villain Tom's truth exposes.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, walking away along a dusty river road at dusk toward the wooded hills above the river.

storyboard.claim: After the trial, the trauma pushes Tom back toward childhood escapism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom walking off down a road toward the hills.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the courtroom to the road.
storyboard.addedInformation: The river road leads toward the limestone hills and the cave.

image.subject: A dark limestone cave with dripping stone walls closing in and a single candle's small light on the wet rock in a narrow passage.

storyboard.claim: The cave is the most claustrophobic sequence in the book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrow dripping cave passage lit by one candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from town to cave.
storyboard.addedInformation: McDougall's cave is a real limestone labyrinth in the hills above the river.

image.subject: A wooded limestone hillside above the broad brown Mississippi, a dark cave mouth among the trees, and an abandoned picnic basket on the grass.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Becky wander from a picnic and get hopelessly lost.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Picnic basket left on the grass, dark cave mouth beyond.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the cave interior to its entrance.
storyboard.addedInformation: The abandoned picnic basket shows how far from safety the two children wandered.

image.subject: A vast dark limestone labyrinth with branching passages and a faint lantern glow far away, oppressive absolute gloom filling the foreground.

storyboard.claim: The cave is a massive uncharted labyrinth of oppressive gloom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Branching black passages, one faint light far off.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the single-passage view to the whole labyrinth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Branching black passages with one far light show the maze the narration calls oppressive.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, holding his last candle aloft in a dark limestone passage, its small flame lighting his face while a girl in a pale blue dress stands behind him.

storyboard.claim: They are out of food and water, and Tom holds his last candle aloft.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom with a single candle raised; Becky behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the cave its human centre.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom raising the last candle shows the boys have no food, water or light left.

image.subject: A small candle stub with a smoking wick stuck on a lump of grey clay against a dark cave wall, its flame sinking toward extinction.

storyboard.claim: The candle wick struggles and expires on a lump of clay.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Candle stub on clay, flame dying.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the candle Tom raised to its death.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dying flame on clay shows the wick running out at its lump of clay.

image.subject: A cold, black cave floor with a snuffed tallow candle and a thin wisp of smoke, absolute darkness all around.

storyboard.claim: They are left in total absolute darkness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Nearly black frame, snuffed candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The candle is gone.
storyboard.addedInformation: A snuffed candle in near-black shows the total darkness the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: Tom's social tools cannot get him out of the cave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text list of the things his charm cannot trade for.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the cave is different from the fence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The list of trades his charm cannot make shows the limits of Tom's social currency.

storyboard.claim: Nature is totally immune to Tom's charisma and storytelling.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list of failed tricks.
storyboard.addedInformation: The plain statement shows that nature ignores the charisma that worked in town.

storyboard.claim: Nature is not the only danger in the cave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement that sets up the threat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the appearance of Injun Joe.
storyboard.addedInformation: The threat line shows a second danger the picture will name next.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, walking down a narrow side passage of a dark cave with a kite string unspooling from his hand back toward a girl sitting in a pale blue dress.

storyboard.claim: Tom leaves Becky resting and explores a side passage with his kite string.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom in a side passage, string running back to Becky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the danger to Tom's action.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kite string running back to Becky shows Tom probing alone away from her.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, peering around a limestone corner, his candle lighting a distant hand that holds another candle.

storyboard.claim: Tom sees a human hand holding a candle and thinks it is a rescuer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at a corner, a second candle-hand ahead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the hope before the reversal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The second candle-hand ahead shows a rescuer as Tom first imagines him.

left.label: HOPE
left.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, beaming and shouting with joy in a dark cave passage.

right.label: DREAD
right.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat, a hard face with a scar, an unshaven jaw and a cold, unblinking stare, turning toward the boy in a dark cave.

storyboard.claim: Tom shouts for joy, then the person turns around and is Injun Joe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Split: the boy's joy against the outlaw's cold stare.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pays off the rescuer hope.
storyboard.addedInformation: The split between the boy's joy and the outlaw's stare shows the reversal in one frame.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat, a hard face with a scar, an unshaven jaw and a cold, unblinking stare, holding a candle close to his face in a dark cave passage.

storyboard.claim: The man is Injun Joe, the man Tom testified against, surely looking for him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe lit by a candle in a dark passage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the reversal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Injun Joe lit in the passage shows the killer Tom testified against, now hunting him.

image.subject: A large grey limestone boulder inside a dark cave with a cross drawn in black candle soot on its face and a stub of candle on the floor beside it.

storyboard.claim: A cross done in candle smoke marks Joe's presence in the cave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Soot cross on a rock, candle stub beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the sign of the threat's presence.
storyboard.addedInformation: The soot cross on the rock shows Joe has marked the cave as his own.

storyboard.claim: Tom is locked in a pitch black labyrinth with a starving murderer; his wit is useless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of stakes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the threat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stakes card shows the trapped boy facing a starving murderer.

storyboard.claim: Is the cave just a standard adventure trope?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only question card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the counter-argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question card shows the cave may be just a cliché of adventure.

storyboard.claim: The cave may be a plot device to show he is brave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the objection in full.
storyboard.addedInformation: The statement shows the cave as a device to prove bravery.

storyboard.claim: The reading of a classic night and shining armor is one the speaker rejects.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only quotation of the adventure-hero phrase.
storyboard.onScreenText: A CLASSIC NIGHT AND SHINING ARMOR
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quotes the trope being rejected.
storyboard.addedInformation: The quoted adventure phrase shows the hero-story reading the narrator rejects.

image.subject: A whitewashed picket fence on a dusty small-town street in summer, a whitewash brush leaning against it, and a dark cave mouth visible on the hill behind.

storyboard.claim: The cave is the dark mirror of the whitewashed fence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fence in sunlight, dark cave mouth on the hill behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the fence to set up the contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: The whitewashed fence is where Tom talked his way out of work.

storyboard.claim: At the fence, talk alters reality; in the cave, talk means nothing and only physical work counts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the contrast.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the mirror.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sunlit fence against the cave shows talk working outside and failing inside.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, cutting rude steps into a steep clay hill inside a cave with a knife, a candle stuck in the wall.

storyboard.claim: Tom cuts steps into the clay so Becky can climb.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom carving steps into clay.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the physical work the speaker described.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom carving steps in the clay shows the physical work that finally counts.

storyboard.claim: Can he really not talk his way out of the cave?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only question card.
storyboard.onScreenText: CAN HE TALK HIS WAY OUT?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the reversal of his behaviour after survival.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question card shows doubt about whether talk can get them out.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, standing on the riverbank looking back up toward the dark cave mouth in the hills.

storyboard.claim: After escaping, Tom goes back to the cave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom on the bank looking back at the cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the escape to the return.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom looking back at the cave shows he cannot leave it behind.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, stepping out of a cave mouth into bright sunlight among trees above the river.

storyboard.claim: He survives the harrowing near-death experience and finds an exit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom emerging into sunlight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the survival that precedes the return.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom in sunlight shows the escape after the near-death ordeal.

image.subject: A heavy plank door with an iron bar and a padlock sealing the mouth of a limestone cave on a hillside above the river.

storyboard.claim: The town seals the cave door, trapping Injun Joe inside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sealed plank door on the cave mouth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the escape to the sealing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door is a town decision, not Tom's.

image.subject: The dry floor of a limestone cave arranged as a hideout, with a plank table, a tin bucket, a coil of rope and a candle in a bottle.

storyboard.claim: With Joe dead and the cave safe, Tom makes the cave his robber gang's hideout.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hideout props on a cave floor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the sealing with the new use.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hideout props show Tom turning the cave into a gang base.

storyboard.claim: Even when faced with brutal reality, Tom's first instinct is to drag it back into play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the thesis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ties back to the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: The statement shows Tom's instinct to turn brutal reality into play.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, and a battered straw-hatted thin barefoot boy in ragged homespun clothes, sitting grinning on a flat rock inside a cave between two tin buckets.

storyboard.claim: Tom turns the trauma into a cool clubhouse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two boys on a rock in the cave, buckets beside them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the play in the same place as the danger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two boys on the rock with buckets show the trauma recast as a clubhouse.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, grinning at the mouth of a limestone cave with a tin bucket in his hand, sunlight on the grass outside.

storyboard.claim: He immediately tries to monetize his trauma as a cool clubhouse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at the cave mouth with a bucket, grinning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the final turn to the buried gold.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom grinning at the cave mouth with a bucket shows him trying to sell the trauma as fun.

image.subject: Two barefoot boys, Tom in a faded blue shirt and Huck in ragged homespun with a battered straw hat, slip through a narrow dark crack in a limestone hillside above a broad brown river at dusk, one carrying a tallow candle.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck sneak back into the cave to hunt the treasure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two boys ducking into a dark cave mouth in the limestone hills, candle flame lighting their faces.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from the essay back to the story: the boys return to the cave.
storyboard.addedInformation: The treasure is Injun Joe's hidden stash.

image.subject: A crude cross drawn in candle soot on a damp limestone wall inside a cave, lit by a single tallow candle held low by an unseen hand, a dark cleft beneath it.

storyboard.claim: Injun Joe marked the spot with a cross in candle soot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A soot-drawn cross on the cave rock, candle glow around it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys reach the marked place under the rock.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cross is the mark that will later frighten Huck.

image.subject: A thin, barefoot 13-year-old boy in ragged homespun clothes, a battered straw hat with a torn brim, dirt on his face, stands frozen in a cave with a shovel dropped at his feet, eyes wide and staring at the dark, candlelight shaking on his face.

storyboard.claim: Huck drops his shovel, terrified that Injun Joe's ghost is near.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Huck rigid in the cave, shovel fallen on the floor, eyes wide with fear.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys reach the cross and the treasure site.
storyboard.addedInformation: Huck believes the murderer's ghost haunts the spot.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, crouched in a cave holding a tallow candle up, a grin half mischief, half calm, as he speaks to a frightened friend.

storyboard.claim: Tom calms Huck by appealing to the town's shared rules about ghosts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom crouched with candle, calm and confident, reasoning with Huck.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Huck is paralysed by superstition.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's skill is turning the town's folklore into argument.

image.subject: Tom, in a faded blue cotton shirt, points up at the crude soot cross on a cave wall while Huck, in ragged clothes, hangs back in the shadows, candlelight between them.

storyboard.claim: Tom argues that a ghost cannot haunt a place marked with a cross.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom pointing at the cross, Huck half-hidden behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom has begun to reason with Huck about the rules.
storyboard.addedInformation: The argument rests on folklore, not evidence.

storyboard.claim: A ghost will not haunt a place with a cross on it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only, the rule stated plainly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's argument from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The logic holds for Huck, which is the point.

image.subject: A dug hole in the cave floor, its dirt pushed aside, with a rotted wooden box opened to reveal a heap of gold coins glinting in candlelight.

storyboard.claim: The boys dig up Injun Joe's buried gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gold coins heaped in a dug hole, candle light on the metal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rule-breaking pays off as they dig.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom literally cashes in on his rebellion.

storyboard.claim: Society forgives rulebreaking once you are rich.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only, a blunt statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The gold has been found.
storyboard.addedInformation: A cynical observation about the town.

image.subject: A dusty 1840s town street of whitewashed picket fences where respectable townsmen in dark Sunday coats and top hats tip their hats to two boys in new, pressed jackets walking with a lifted stride.

storyboard.claim: The town suddenly welcomes the two boys now that they are rich.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townsmen tipping hats to Tom and Huck in new jackets on a town street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The gold makes the boys acceptable.
storyboard.addedInformation: Their mischief is forgotten because of wealth.

storyboard.claim: The gold totals $6,000, split half for Tom and half for Huck.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Large figure $6,000 with a split label.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payout is now quantified.
storyboard.addedInformation: Widow Douglas and Judge Thatcher will invest the money at 6% interest.

image.subject: A bank ledger open on a polished wooden counter in a tidy 1840s office, a pen laid across a column of figures, the page showing a sum of 6 percent interest.

storyboard.claim: Six percent of $3,000 is about $180 a year.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ledger page with interest figures.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The $6,000 is invested at 6 percent.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boys' income is calculated from the invested half.

storyboard.claim: The boys have an income of a dollar a day plus a weekday.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Stat figure $1 a day.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The interest is turned into income.
storyboard.addedInformation: Twain notes it matches the minister's promised pay.

image.subject: A single silver dollar coin resting on a worn leather Bible on a wooden pulpit in a small country church, with a dim window light falling across both.

storyboard.claim: A dollar a day is what the town minister was promised, rarely collected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A silver dollar on a Bible on a pulpit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys' income matches the minister's.
storyboard.addedInformation: The minister rarely actually collected his pay.

storyboard.claim: The boys now hold the liquid assets and income of the town's moral authority.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three short items listed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The money has been invested.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boys match the town's most respected man.

storyboard.claim: Does getting rich ruin the whole point of the book?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only, the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The wealth raises a question about the book's theme.
storyboard.addedInformation: The next beat answers it.

image.subject: Judge Thatcher, a dignified man in his fifties in a black frock coat and white high collar with grey side-whiskers, signs a ledger at a writing desk in a timber bank office while two boys in new jackets watch from a bench.

storyboard.claim: The boys hand their money to the judge to invest, becoming capitalists.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Judge Thatcher at a desk signing a ledger, boys watching.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The money goes into the system.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boys join the establishment through investment.

storyboard.claim: The boys did not become the establishment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only, the blunt answer.
storyboard.onScreenText: THEY DID NOT JOIN THE ESTABLISHMENT
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question about the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reaction to the money reveals who they are.

image.subject: A thin, barefoot 13-year-old boy in stiff, unfamiliar new clothes with a high collar, sitting awkwardly at a set dinner table in a tidy house, holding a fork in one hand with a sour, sly, watchful expression.

storyboard.claim: Huck explicitly hates being respectable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Huck stiff and uncomfortable at a set table with a fork.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Respectability is shown as a fact of the boys' new life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Huck's discomfort shows his real nature.

image.subject: An old wooden hogshead barrel lying on a muddy riverbank, a ragged bedroll and a battered straw hat set beside it, the broad brown river behind.

storyboard.claim: Huck runs from the widow's clean bed and wants to sleep in a hogshead.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A barrel on the riverbank with a bedroll.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Huck rejects the clean bed.
storyboard.addedInformation: The barrel is Huck's preferred home.

left.label: CLEAN BED
left.subject: A made bed with starched white sheets and a stiff pillow in a tidy house bedroom.

right.label: HOGSHEAD
right.subject: An old wooden hogshead barrel on the riverbank with a ragged bedroll inside.

storyboard.claim: Huck prefers the hogshead to the clean bed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two sleeping places side by side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Huck's rejection of respectability.
storyboard.addedInformation: Huck chooses freedom over comfort.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, now neatly brushed, leans over an old wooden hogshead barrel by the river, peering inside where a ragged, dirt-faced boy in a battered straw hat hides.

storyboard.claim: Tom tracks Huck down in his hiding place and urges him back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom peering into the barrel where Huck hides.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Huck is hiding in the hogshead.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom wants Huck to return to the widow's house.

storyboard.claim: Why does Tom care whether Huck is respectable?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only, the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom asks Huck to go back and be good.
storyboard.addedInformation: The answer is in the next beat.

storyboard.claim: Tom's robber gang must have high standards.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three gang rules as a checklist.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom answers his own question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gang needs respectability to look good in the town's eyes.

image.subject: A black cloth mask and a small heap of gold coins on a rough wooden table in a dim cabin, a tallow candle burning beside them.

storyboard.claim: Tom uses the town's respectability rules to fund his anti-society games.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask cloth and gold coins on a table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's gang needs respectability as cover.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gold pays for the game.

image.subject: A long oak table where stern elderly men in black frock coats sit around a ledger, while a barefoot boy in a pressed jacket slides a gold coin across the polished wood toward them.

storyboard.claim: Tom uses wealth to insulate himself and play on his own terms.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Town elders at a table with a boy sliding a coin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's money gives him influence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom buys control of the town's respectable men.

image.subject: A tall stack of gold coins on a wooden tabletop beside a folded, unopened town ordinance book, a candle casting long shadows.

storyboard.claim: Tom never submitted to the town's values, he simply acquired his own capital.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Coins stacked beside an unopened rulebook.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payment and influence are summed up.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's money lets him ignore the town's rules.

storyboard.claim: Tom forces the town to agree to his terms: whitewash, dead rats, then gold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step timeline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises Tom's tactics.
storyboard.addedInformation: Each tactic is a step up in leverage.

image.subject: An open novel with a cracked spine lying on a schoolroom desk beside a pen and a worn slate, a single window throwing light across the pages.

storyboard.claim: The book itself has real flaws worth acknowledging.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open book on a school desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from praise to critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: The critique begins with the book's structure.

image.subject: A brass balance scale on a wooden table, a stack of gold coins on one pan and a closed book on the other, the pans level.

storyboard.claim: Tom's economic hacking is brilliant, but the book has flaws.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Scales with coins and a book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The counterpoint is weighed against the praise.
storyboard.addedInformation: Both sides are real.

image.subject: A bundle of loosely bound printed pages spread unevenly across a wooden desk, a pen laid across the top sheet, a small pile of pages slipping off the edge.

storyboard.claim: The book feels less like a tightly plotted novel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Loose pages spilling on a desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the counterpoint.
storyboard.addedInformation: The structure feels episodic.

image.subject: An empty painted stage with faded velvet curtains pulled to each side, a single wooden stool in the spotlight, dust hanging in the light.

storyboard.claim: The book is a series of loosely strung vaudeville sketches.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty stage under a spotlight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the structural critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Episodes feel like separate turns on a stage.

image.subject: A small white curly-haired poodle trotting down the aisle of a plain country church, past rows of startled townsfolk in dark Sunday coats, while a grinning boy in a faded blue shirt watches from a pew.

storyboard.claim: A church scene with a pinch bug and a poodle becomes a chaotic comedy routine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A poodle running down a church aisle past startled congregation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives a concrete example of the vaudeville feel.
storyboard.addedInformation: The episode is funny but does not move the plot.

image.subject: An empty wooden bench in a schoolhouse with a closed slate lying on it, dusty light falling through a window onto the bare floor.

storyboard.claim: The episode does not drive the plot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty bench with a slate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the example of the poodle episode.
storyboard.addedInformation: Some episodes are only for laughs.

left.label: TENDER
left.subject: A stout, grey-haired woman in a dark calico dress with a white collar and apron, spectacles on a cord, gently holding a boy's chin in a sunlit kitchen.

right.label: CRUEL
right.subject: A ragged, unkempt outcast man sitting alone on a cold stone step in a dim alley, his hands hanging between his knees.

storyboard.claim: Twain swings between saccharine tenderness and a cynical depiction of the poor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two contrasting pictures of tenderness and outcast life.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the tonal swings.
storyboard.addedInformation: The outcast's plight is treated harshly.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, wearing a torn grey shirt and stained trousers, sits in a dim stone jail cell with a chain at his wrist, his head bowed.

storyboard.claim: The book frames Muff Potter harshly, a grim and sad figure in a cell.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff Potter seated in a cell, chained at the wrist.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the outcast a face for the tonal swing.
storyboard.addedInformation: He is a victim of the town's judgment.

storyboard.claim: A Sunday school episode leaves a boy permanently harmed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only, the place named.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Another harsh tonal shift.
storyboard.addedInformation: The harm is shown as aftermath, not on screen.

image.subject: An open, worn novel lying on a wooden raft tied to a river bank at dusk, the broad brown Mississippi moving quietly behind it.

storyboard.claim: Huckleberry Finn has tighter psychological depth than Tom Sawyer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open book on a raft at the river.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the sequel comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sequel is a different and deeper kind of book.

image.subject: A thin, barefoot 13-year-old boy in ragged homespun clothes stands at the tiller of a raft on the dark river at night, a lantern glowing at his feet and his face turned toward the far shore.

storyboard.claim: In Huck's story the episodic journey mirrors his moral struggle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Huck on a raft at night with a lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the comparison with Huckleberry Finn.
storyboard.addedInformation: Huck's moral reflection is deep and personal.

image.subject: A small wooden stage under a single hanging candle lantern, a freckled boy in a faded blue shirt standing center with a theatrical bow, and empty benches stretched out in front in the dark.

storyboard.claim: Tom is always performing on a stage rather than living inside his head.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy bowing on a small stage before empty benches.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The comparison leads to Tom's opacity.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book is a performance.

image.subject: A long whitewashed picket fence along a dusty street in a humid, sun-bleached 1840s river town on a Saturday morning, a freckled boy in a faded blue shirt and bare feet holding a whitewash brush beside it.

storyboard.claim: The opening scene is the humid Saturday morning and the whitewashed fence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom beside the whitewashed fence with a brush.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the opening image of the book.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the reframing of the fence.

image.subject: A round-faced 12-year-old boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, eating a crisp red apple, leaning on a whitewashed picket fence on a dusty St. Petersburg street on a bright summer morning, a cheerful and gullible grin.

storyboard.claim: The gullible boys who paid Tom with apples and kites are the scene we laugh at.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben Rogers, apple in hand, at the fence in the sun.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the opening fence scene the book closes on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the exact boy the narrator means, so the reversal lands on a face.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat with a neutral, thoughtful expression, standing by a whitewashed picket fence and looking at it as if seeing it for the first time, in soft afternoon light.

storyboard.claim: Maybe the boys who were conned were not fools after all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An adult pausing at the fence, rethinking it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the laugh of the previous line into a second look.
storyboard.addedInformation: A viewer sees the reader's own reassessment in the figure.

image.subject: Three barefoot boys in patched shirts line up at a whitewashed fence, handing over a kite, a tin bucket and a red apple to a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt who holds a whitewash brush and grins, a dusty street behind them in the morning sun.

storyboard.claim: The boys were paying for the privilege of an exclusive chance to take part.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boys queuing to hand over treasures for a brush.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the boys were not fools, moving from doubt to a purchase.
storyboard.addedInformation: The barter is shown as an eager line, not a con.

image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt and patched knee trousers, barefoot, perched on top of a whitewashed picket fence and gazing down the dusty main street of St. Petersburg, a half-mischief grin on his face.

storyboard.claim: Tom understood the town better than anyone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom perched above the street, surveying the town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the boys to the boy who manages them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places Tom above the town, which fits the claim he read it best.

image.subject: A stack of pale Sunday school tickets fanned across a plain wooden schoolroom table beside a lit tallow candle, with a worn Bible at one end, in warm candlelit light.

storyboard.claim: Work, play and heroism are stories we agree to believe, not laws of nature.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tickets fanned on a table, worth only what the town agrees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the currency of the town's shared agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tickets carry the idea that value is agreed, not physical.

storyboard.claim: Value is a community agreement, and Tom was the master storyteller.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quotation card with the thesis line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Distills the previous beat into the book's thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: A real quotable line, so the text carries it without a picture.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat stands at a whitewashed picket fence on a sunlit street, watching a barefoot boy in a faded blue shirt with a whitewash brush paint the fence while the adult's hand rests on his own coat pocket, a thoughtful half-smile.

storyboard.claim: Consider Tom as you deal with your own week, office politics and chores.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grown adult watching a boy work the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the story toward the viewer's own week.
storyboard.addedInformation: The adult stands in for the viewer, watching the trick happen.

image.subject: A prosperous merchant in a black frock coat and white high collar counts gold coins at a polished wooden counter in a dim 1840s general store, a ledger open beside him and a lantern glowing on the shelf behind.

storyboard.claim: Tom is the prototype for the Gilded Age American businessman.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A merchant counting gold at a store counter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the businessman the narrator names a face.
storyboard.addedInformation: Period-correct props (gold, ledger, lantern) make the businessman concrete.

storyboard.claim: Tom was the original marketer, creating demand out of thin air.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A short punchline card, no picture needed.
storyboard.onScreenText: The original marketer: demand out of thin air.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sharpens the businessman point into a single line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the trick plainly in a sentence the viewer can hold.

image.subject: An ordinary adult in a plain grey coat stands in the open doorway of a plain clapboard house at dusk, looking out at a dusty street lined with whitewashed picket fences, the lamps just lit.

storyboard.claim: Look around your own life at the structures you buy into.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A doorway at dusk, looking out at the town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the thesis by asking the viewer to look at their own structures.
storyboard.addedInformation: The open doorway frames the viewer stepping out to look.
